speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In my Statement today, I will explain the Government's fuller considerations for making this move and set out the next steps forward.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our history is an integral part of our identity as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Current and future generations of Singaporeans need to know where we came from, the challenges we have overcome together and the sacrifices our forefathers have made to build Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: When we are grounded in our history and we share a strong identity, we will build our future purposefully as one people, one nation, one Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Historic sites, buildings and structures connect us to our past and to our heritage.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: They bear witness to historic events that shaped our nation and allow us to be in the same space as the people who played key roles in shaping our history.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: NHB is the Government body charged with the role of preserving these historic sites and buildings under the PMA.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It ensures that our National Monuments remain in our urban fabric and are present in our collective memory as physical representations of key milestones in Singapore's historic development.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We have gazetted historic buildings as National Monuments, like the Former Parliament House and the Former City Hall.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We have also gazetted the Padang site as a National Monument because it has hosted key historical events, including our first National Day Parade in 1966 and celebrations of the installation of Singapore's first Yang di-Pertuan Negara Encik Yusof bin Ishak.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: They collectively convey different aspects of the Singapore Story and identity.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Some represent our religious diversity while others are important civic and cultural buildings.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Most have their roots from the colonial period.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Only a precious few, like the ones I shared earlier, embody Singapore's struggle for self-determination after the Second World War, and our aspirations as a newly independent nation post-1965.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We therefore need to carefully steward monuments that reflect this phase in our national history, and protect this cultural inheritance for our future generations.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: They collectively connect Singaporeans with our Singapore Story.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In land-scarce Singapore, preservation is something we enter into only after a rigorous assessment process administered by NHB.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: NHB conducts thorough research on the history and significance of the identified site, including the events and people associated with the site, as well as their impact on the trajectory of Singapore's history.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This research is then assessed by the Preservation of Sites and Monuments Advisory Board (PSMAB).

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This is an independent board consisting experts in fields relevant to National Monuments, such as history and architecture.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The PSMAB considers the merits of each case holistically and objectively, based on its historical significance, architectural and design merit, and authenticity.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: If the PSMAB finds the identified building or site to be worthy of preservation and NHB supports the assessment, NHB will submit its recommendation to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth for decision.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: If the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth agrees with the recommendation, a Notice of Intention will be issued to notify the owner and occupier of the site of the Government's intention to preserve the building or site.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And as stated under the law, the owner and occupier will be provided a reasonable period to submit any objections to the intended preservation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: NHB will consider all objections received and make further recommendations on whether to proceed with this preservation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Thereafter, the Government will make a final decision on whether to proceed with the preservation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The matter has received considerable attention over the years and extensive discussions in this House.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I will not recount the background in detail, but let me do a quick recap of the salient points.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: First, it was Mr Lee Kuan Yew's preference for the house on 38 Oxley Road to be demolished.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It was also Mdm Kwa's wish for the family's living spaces to remain private.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Second, Mr Lee understood that he had to abide by the processes and the systems that he had built, and that the Government has a duty and a responsibility to consider the public interest, and not just those of private individuals.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And that was why on 27 December 2011, he had written to the Cabinet, and he had stated, and I quote, "If 38 Oxley Road is to be preserved, it needs to have its foundations reinforced and the whole building refurbished.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It must then be let out for people to live in.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: An empty building will soon decline and decay." In March 2012, he had also applied to the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) to renovate the house.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This would had kept the structure of the original house and added other spaces to it.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Third, there was no need to make any decision on 38 Oxley Road prior to this, as Dr Lee Wei Ling was residing in the house.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: NHB and PSMAB have since completed the process to determine the site's eligibility and suitability for preservation under the PMA, and NHB has made its recommendation to me as Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For this case, public officers on PSMAB recused themselves during the assessment to ensure that the site was considered independently.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: They note that the site bore witness to pivotal events in the 1950s that marked Singapore's transition from a colony to an independent nation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The site also served as the venue for conversations, activities and decisions of our founding leaders, which profoundly influenced the trajectory of Singapore's independence movement and our subsequent national history.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It was the gathering point for activists and trade unionists who came to seek help and legal consultations with Mr Lee.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It also hosted regular meetings, often in the basement dining room, where key individuals such as Dr Goh Keng Swee, Dr Toh Chin Chye, Mr S Rajaratnam and Mr KM Byrne discussed the feasibility of forming a political party to contest the Legislative Assembly elections.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: These meetings progressively grew to include other individuals involved in the anti-colonial struggle, such as Mr Lim Chin Siong and Mr Fong Swee Suan, who later split away to form the Barisan Sosialis.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Prominent Malayan leaders like Tunku Abdul Rahman and Tan Cheng Lock also visited the site for discussions.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The site witnessed discussions where these key individuals formulated their vision, plans and values for Singapore, leading to the formation of the People's Action Party and its landslide victory in the 1959 Legislative Assembly Elections, resulting in Singapore's first fully independent Government.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This makes the site a unique and foundational part of the story of Singapore's independence.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And hence, the PSMAB concluded that the site is of national importance with great historic merit.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: If preserved, the site would allow current and future generations of Singaporeans to reflect upon these significant events and the ideals and the values that have shaped Singapore.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: It is the confluence of people, place and events that gives a site its historical significance.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We have very few such sites in Singapore where there is such a confluence.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And 38 Oxley Road is one of them.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: As a young nation, we need to retain this unique site for it bears witness to the birth of independent Singapore and to key moments in our history.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Preserving the site means we will be able to avoid a situation where private parties attempt to purchase 38 Oxley Road in future, just to have an address that is associated with Mr Lee's residence.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I am sure all of us in this House and the vast majority of Singaporeans will want to make sure that that situation does not happen.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: I would also like to clarify that the Government's considerations were for the entire site, and not for the buildings or structures within it.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Preserving the site does not obligate the Government to keep the buildings and structures within the site in their current condition.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In fact, the relevant authorities have not had the chance to enter the site to assess the conditions of the buildings and the structures.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And that is a key reason why we are opting to preserve the site, rather than just specific buildings or structures.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: If access to the site is obtained, the Government will undertake a detailed study of the buildings and the structures within the site.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will take into account factors like the existing condition and weigh the potential benefit of retaining them against the costs.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The Government will consider all options, including those proposed by the Ministerial Committee on 38 Oxley Road in 2018 which include partial or full demolitions of the buildings and structures.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Regardless of the option taken, the Government will respect Mr Lee and Mdm Kwa's wishes to protect their family's privacy by removing all traces of their private living spaces from the interior of the house.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Under no circumstance will the interior of the house, as Mr Lee and Mdm Kwa knew, be displayed or recorded or remodelled or duplicated elsewhere.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In fact, many other countries around the world have preserved and converted sites associated with their nation's independence as spaces for public education and appreciation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: For example, there is the Gandhi Ashram in India.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This marks the site where Mahatma Gandhi lived from 1917 to 1930 and was the centre of Gandhi's non-violent resistance movement against British colonial rule of India.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: There is also the Independence National Historical Park in the United States (US), which includes buildings that witnessed the country's key historic milestones, like the signing of the Declaration of Independence and the US Constitution.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In many such instances, they have made changes to the sites, including modifying or adapting the original buildings with new interpretive structures to better enable the public to experience the site as a park or a heritage space.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: And that is why we are keeping an open mind as to the treatment of the buildings and the structures within the site.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will keep all options open and strive for a solution that will unite us as a country, rather than allow this to become a point of contention or division in our society.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In the interim, there will be no public access to 38 Oxley Road.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Following the service of the Notice of Intention, due process under the PMA will be accorded to the owner and any occupier.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In line with existing practice, a notice period of 14 calendar days will be provided for them to submit objections to the NHB.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: NHB will then submit any objections received and their recommendations to me, in the capacity of Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth, to decide whether to proceed with the preservation of the site.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: All objections submitted and recommendations made will be considered objectively and fairly as part of due process.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Such acquisition will be done in accordance with established processes and compensation will be made in accordance with the Land Acquisition Act.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The owner, any occupiers and any other persons interested will be given the opportunity to submit their claims to the Singapore Land Authority (SLA) to determine the compensation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: A professional private valuer will also be appointed to assist SLA in determining the market value of the land, taking into consideration any claims submitted.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: If the owner or any person interested is not satisfied with the compensation awarded, a Notice of Appeal can be filed with the Land Acquisition Appeals Board.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: If preserved, the acquisition will allow the Government to take all necessary steps to safeguard the site and preserve it in keeping with its historic significance and national importance.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: (In Mandarin):   National identity is the bedrock of a nation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Especially for a young nation like Singapore, we must ensure that this and future generations are deeply rooted in our history and our sense of self.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: What the Government is preserving is not just any particular building, but a site which has witnessed an important part of our road to Independence.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: What we are remembering is not a leader, but our struggle towards independence.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This is something that is not represented by any other site or monument.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The Government intends to preserve the site, but this does not mean the buildings will be kept in exactly the same form.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will study the sensitive and suitable treatment of the structures on site to turn the site into a potential place for educating our young on our national history so that they have a deeper understanding of what it means to be a Singaporean.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Yesterday's Lianhe Zaobao editorial pointed out that the Government's decision is based on national interests.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The preservation of the site seeks to ensure that the story of our nation-building journey lives on for generations to come. : Mr Speaker, Sir, the Government has arrived at this approach for 38 Oxley Road, because this is the most responsible approach.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In its 2018 report, the Ministerial Committee on 38 Oxley Road stated that a future government will have to make an informed and considered decision on the matter when it becomes necessary.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: This is the future government, and the time is now.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We will take the deliberate steps to decide and we will do so in the best interest of Singapore and Singaporeans now and for the future.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Our history and journey from immigrants with no rights to an independent country of Singapore Citizens is fought for by key people and through key events that shaped our destiny.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: The physical spaces that bore witness to these events are our only links to these pivotal moments in our history.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: There will come a time when no one who has lived through Singapore's struggle for independence will be around to recount these stories first-hand, but the sights and markers that we choose to keep today will continue to speak for them.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: They will remind us of our hard-fought path to become a multiracial, multireligious and sovereign nation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: In preserving the site, we are not memorialising any single leader.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We are safeguarding the grounds where future generations can stand to understand where we came from, who we are and what we overcame together.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: We do this so that our children, our grandchildren and their children after them will know the story of Singapore, not as something distant or abstract, but as something lived, earned and entrusted to them.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
text: Then, our Singapore spirit will endure and it will grow stronger with every generation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But before I call hon Members for clarifications, I wish to point out that pursuant to Standing Order 23, Members may seek clarification on the Ministerial Statement, but no debate shall be allowed thereon.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In other words, no long mini speeches as well.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Members can seek clarifications by way of asking questions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I seek Members' understanding to keep your clarifications clear and concise so that the Minister can answer as many clarifications as possible.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We had an intense debate on this in the same House in 2017.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Given the same sensitivities surrounding 38 Oxley Road, will the Government consider structured public engagement or consultation when developing the interpretative plans to ensure that the eventual design fosters unity and avoids reopening old political disputes?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For the sake of public clarity, could the Minister outline the key project milestones that Singaporeans can expect from now until the final configuration, if the site is decided to be preserved?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Lastly, Sir, Minister has also taken pains to explain that the preservation decision concerns national memory and not personalities.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Could the Minister elaborate how the Government will communicate this to the public so as to avoid misconception that this is an attempt to memorialise any individual rather than our shared independence journey?

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: This is something we do with all our National Monuments.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: Some of the possible stakeholder groups include heritage enthusiasts and educators, to ensure that the site can enhance their efforts to enhance public education of our history.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: Other groups that could potentially be engaged would also include people who represent target demographic groups, for example, the youths or our seniors, to ensure that the stories and the memories are also captured within the use of the site.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And most importantly, like I mentioned in my Ministerial Statement, we want to ensure that some of these stories are able to be handed down to the next generation and the generation after that.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: Given the technical expertise of the PSMAB in these fields, including history, architecture and conservation, the advisory board will also be consulted to ensure that the treatment of the buildings and the structures on the site befit the historical importance and the national significance of this site.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: To the Member's second clarification about key project milestones, Sir, I had earlier outlined to Members some of these key milestones from the issuance of the Notice of Intention to the intended acquisition of the site, if a Preservation Order is made.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: This will inform our study on the potential options for future uses of the site, which will also include a holistic assessment on the impact of the surrounding neighbourhood, including possible options for public access, parking, traffic impact.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And as I mentioned earlier, we will also conduct engagements with stakeholders and residents, and take in their feedback on the eventual use and the design of the site.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: For the Member's third clarification regarding how we will communicate this, especially to younger Singaporeans that this is something that intends to commemorate our shared independence journey.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: As I mentioned earlier in my Ministerial Statement, the reason why the PSMAB has recommended the site for preservation is because of its close association with our struggle for self-government in the 1950s, and this is a very rare location, where it is place, people and events – the confluence – and it is also something that is associated with most, if not, all the key participants in this anti-colonial struggle.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: The focus of this education, therefore, is on the pivotal historical events that happened there, one that brought us from colonial to self-rule to independence, rather than the lives of those people who lived there.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It is not just because this is his personal wish but also the values that he espouse, which is not to have personal monuments.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, my first question to the Minister is whether the Government has taken this aspect into consideration in coming to the decision?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Can I ask the Minister would the Founders' Memorial be able to encapsulate the historical and national significance of our founding values and ideals, without having to preserve 38 Oxley Road?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And thirdly, in the light of NHB's recommendation and MCCY's decision, can I ask the Minister if he can update if there has been any change in the Government's policy position with regard to preserving and creating National Monuments?

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: As I stated in my Ministerial Statement, Mr Lee clearly wanted to protect the privacy of his family.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And Mr Lee was also quite adamant in his life that he did not want to be idolised or memorialised, and therefore I believe that the approach as outlined in my Ministerial Statement is the best for way forward, given the circumstances.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: Because given the site's historic significance and national importance, the Government has a duty to consider this, not just from the lens of a private individual, but also from a good public policy lens – what is good for current and future Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: It is our duty to allow future Singaporeans to have the opportunity to visit the site and to appreciate the gravity of discussions that took place at the site, discussions that brought us to our independence.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And we are also clear that it is our intention that we are not preserving the site and using it to showcase the personal effects of Mr Lee or his family.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: We are focusing on the nationally significant events that took place at the site and not memorialising his life.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: In keeping an open mind regarding the buildings and the structures, we would then be able to best consider how best to strike the balance between preserving the historical significance of the site and maximising its public value to Singaporeans, and respecting Mr Lee's wishes.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: What is unique is that it gives us an opportunity to stand on the same grounds and be in the very same space where pivotal events in national history took place and we are walking in the same footsteps of those who came before us.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And therefore, it provides us with a certain frame of reference, a certain sense of place, to appreciate how far we have come.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: That is also the reason why we have preserved several sites in Singapore, such as City Hall, Padang and more recently, the former Kandang Kerbau Hospital, as they help us and the future generations recollect and connect with this critical history that we share as a nation.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: This sense of place, this being in the same space as those who came before us, it is not something that can be captured by replication at another site.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: The Founders' Memorial is a site that is reconstructed.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: It does not share that same sense of place, that same place that housed all the critical events.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: The Founders' Memorial is a place that is meant to allow our future generations to learn from the shared values that our founding generation, had which is quite different from the site of 38 Oxley Road.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And if preserved, this site will then help to augment the Founders' Memorial by providing a site that gives our visitors a first-hand appreciation of the things that took place at the very same site and provides that historical context and background to some of these ideals that the Founders' Memorial is commemorating.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: The NHB and the Government has always sought to identify sites of national significance to be assessed as potential National Monuments, particularly if they attest to parts, key parts, pivotal parts of our national history that is under-represented by existing National Monuments.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: As a young nation in our 60th year, it is not unexpected that most of our National Monuments originate from before our independence.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: But this also means, like I mentioned in my Ministerial Statement, sites that attest to our founding independence and our nation building, there are only those a very precious few, which is why it is so important for us to look at this site with all the full considerations of handing it down to future generations, and what is good for Singapore and Singaporeans, both current and future.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And as important events in our national history, it is important that we continue to look for these sites and to preserve them if they are assessed to be worthy in a way that can allow it to better contribute back to society and to enhance the public's appreciation of some of these very pivotal events.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, given that the Government already intends to issue a Preservation Order to gazette 38 Oxley Road as a National Monument, why is there still a need for the Government to acquire the site?

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In other words, it is not about the private life of Mr Lee Kuan Yew, but about the fight for independence of our people.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: For example, the Government has the resources and the expertise at its disposal to ensure that the site is properly maintained and it is maintained in a manner that will be able to benefit Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: This is the most responsible course of action to ensure that our future generations of Singaporeans can appreciate the significance of the site, and it can be a part of a collective memory and help to build our shared identity.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: On the second question, the point-blank question, well, I want to restate, as I had stated in my Ministerial Statement that the site has been objectively and independently assessed by the PSMAB.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And I would also like to quote the Statement of Assessment by the PSMAB, "the site was more than just the home of Singapore's founding Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew, who lived and worked there from 1950 until his death in 2015.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: It bore witness to pivotal events in the 1950s that marked Singapore's transition from a colony to an independent nation.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: The modest buildings contrast with the impactful and consequential decisions taken there." It is very clear that the historical significance of this site is not solely about Mr Lee Kuan Yew.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: The individuals that participated in these meetings and the discussions at the site, they came from across the political spectrum.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: So, the reason for the preservation of the site is because it bore witness to pivotal events that brought Singapore from colonial to self-rule to our independence as a sovereign nation.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, this matter has been very long running.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am glad that the Government is making efforts to bring this chapter to a close.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Minister said that the Government intends to conclude its plan for the site, "well within this term of Government." Can the Minister provide more clarity on the timeline moving forward?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In terms of: the possible acquisition, further study needed to be done and the Government's final decision.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My second question, I understand that one of the possible outcomes for 38 Oxley Road is to turn it into a heritage park.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While we understand that further study and planning have yet to be conducted, would the Minister be able to share the following and I have got the following points.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The second point is, if residents in the immediate vicinity be one of the parties who will be consulted, but I think just now Minister did mention that they will be consulted, so I thank Minister for that.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My third point, Oxley is a very narrow road and there is a lot of illegal parking in the surrounding condominiums too.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I would like to know if any potential impact to the traffic parking and congestion of the surrounding areas be seriously studied and considered as well.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: Under the law, the owner and the occupier of the site has to be given a reasonable period to raise any objections and then, thereafter, the Government has to carefully consider any such objections before deciding whether to make a Preservation Order on the site.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: Therefore, it is very premature for the Government to commit to any timelines in terms of the future milestones and timelines.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And this is also the point that I made in my Ministerial Statement, where I said my colleagues and the relevant technical experts have not had access to the site for quite a while.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: If the site is preserved and acquired, like I said earlier for the first clarification, our agencies will conduct a holistic feasibility study on the potential options and the future use.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: That is not just for the use of the site within itself, but it also includes other agencies, such as the Land Transport Authority, to look into things, such as the traffic impact, parking impact, public access, so that this is more holistic.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And then, we can look at doing it in a way that befits its importance and significance, and in a way that allows the public to be able to appreciate the site and at the same time, not create disamenities.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: We will also engage residents, and we will consider their feedback as part of this process.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And we will also be very happy to work with the Member, if acquired, if preserved, on how to be able to develop this site in a way that is in harmony with its surroundings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Nevertheless, we have received neither requests nor guidance to speak on this matter, and the statements and questions that follow are entirely our own.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I understand the fundamental policy tension that the advisory board must confront: the site has clear significant historical meaning for our nation and in this sense, it is as much private property as it is one that metaphorically belongs to all of us; and also, the Government has previously intervened to gazette private property as National Monuments in the past, so in this regard, the decision is not unprecedented.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: However, the personal desire of Mr Lee Kuan Yew, the original owner, to demolish the site is well-known as well as the application by the site's current owner, Mr Lee Hsien Yang, to proceed with the demolition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I note that the Government has yet to decide on whether, gazette notwithstanding, the site's buildings and structures will be preserved in the present form.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And I also note the preservation will take at least the minimal step of removing all private living spaces, in accordance with Mr Lee Kuan Yew's wishes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My clarifications may be bucketed into two main themes: first, how NHB weighs the tension between public benefits and private preferences in their deliberations; and second, the options NHB is considering going forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: On the first question, will the Minister share if there is a system that the advisory board follows in evaluating public interest versus private ones, prior to invoking eminent domain to gazette a site?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: How are significant elements, such as the property's architectural value or socio-cultural significance weighed against development considerations, such as potential future land use and development restrictions implied by the gazette?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: How much weight would the preferences of the owner for how the property should be treated, since there have, historically, never been any previous objections to an intended gazette?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: On the second, will the Government consider future course of action for the site that heavily favours privacy, while preserving the decision to gazette?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In particular, will it not consider not demolishing the buildings, but nevertheless, closing the site to visitors, unless explicit permission of the current owner has been granted?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Alternatively, will the Government consider dismantling the site's main structures and reconstructing these at the Founders' Memorial?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: These approaches strike me as more respectful of both the public interest benefit of preserving elements of the site for posterity, while also accommodating the private property rights of the owner to do with the property as he or she wishes.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: So, there is no policy tension on their part.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: They do not consider other things, like individuals' wishes; they are just scoring it based on technical merit.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: These criteria are all based on international best practices for heritage assessments.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: The PSMAB will first consider if the identified site is nationally significant, such as whether it is directly linked to key events or people who have had a significant impact on our history.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: If it is assessed to have national significance, the PSMAB would then deliberate the site's historic and design merit from a technical perspective.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: For example, sites that have been assessed to be deeply relevant to these historic events or individuals would have to be considered to have strong historic merit.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And sites which have been assessed to be of national significance and of exceptional historic and/or architectural design merit would then be considered worthy of preservation.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: I think the second point is that, as I mentioned in my Ministerial Statement, our colleagues and our technical experts have not had the chance to visit the site.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: So, some of those options that the Member suggested could well be possible.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: But at this point in time, it is premature to comment.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: (In Mandarin):   First of all, I would like to thank the Acting Minister for explaining very clearly the development options for 38 Oxley Road.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I have three questions regarding 38 Oxley Road, the preservation of the home of Mr Lee Kuan Yew and how it will be handled.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Given its historical, cultural and national significance, what objective criteria and expert consultations has the Government used in accessing the property’s heritage value?

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Thirdly, will the Government consider establishing an independent advisory team that will comprise historians, architects and community representatives to make recommendations on the future use of 38 Oxley Road, so as to foster social consensus?

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: On the first question, when it comes to the objective standards and independent assessments, I think I had sort of covered those in my response to the hon Member Assoc Prof Jamus Lim; and I would not repeat those answers here.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: On the second question about how we ensure that this decision process is in the public interest and it is done in an open, transparent and accountable way, if the site is preserved as a National Monument, our agencies will engage with all the relevant stakeholders, such as heritage enthusiasts, educators, conservation experts as well as some of the target demographic groups, like youths, seniors, to explore possible options for the future use of the site.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: Therefore, this whole process will be something that is open, transparent and it also ensures that it will be accountable.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And then, given their technical expertise in fields, including history, architecture, conservation, the PSMAB will also be consulted to make sure that the treatment of the buildings and the structures of the site befit the assessed historical significance and national importance.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: On the third point about forming an independent committee, I think covered that in the second clarification.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: This is also similar to the clarifications I have given to Member Mr Alex Yam as well as Member Joan Pereira, that we will be involving Members, relevant technical experts as well as important stakeholders and some members of the public in consultations to look at the future use of the site.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: On the practical note, may I ask the Minister if the Landed Housing Areas zoning of the area will remain unchanged or will there be a review of zoning rules in the neighbourhood?

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: My second question to the Acting Minister, is it truly necessary to arrive at a decision on what to do with this site in this term of Government?

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: I ask this because of my disquiet at some of the options listed in the 2018 Ministerial Committee report, which included options to demolish everything except the basement dining room.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: We must remember that what is demolished cannot be undemolished.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: I note that the Ministerial Committee report also noted that there may be a loss of historical context under this option.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: Would it not be better to leave these decisions on future developments of the site to future generations?

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: On the clarification about area zoning, as I mentioned in my Ministerial Statement, while the Government intends to preserve the site, there is still a due process that the Government has to follow as required of us under the Act.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: Until a decision on this preservation has been made, it will be quite premature for the Government to review the planning and development controls for the neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: I agree with the Member that we should make an informed and considered decision, because what is demolished, what option is taken away, can never be brought back.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: But at the same time, I think this Government has a duty to make a deliberate decision to decide.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: It will be an informed and considered decision.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Lee Kuan Yew was our founding Prime Minister and played an important role in Singapore's nation-building journey.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Many residents I have spoken to describe Mr Lee Kuan Yew as the nation's "Founding Father".

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Government actively take measures to continuously remind the public of the importance of this place to Singapore's history and culture?

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: On her first clarification about the significant role of this site.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: If the site is preserved and acquired, we will leverage on it to educate the current and future generations on this significant part of Singapore's history.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And this is the main reason why the Government intends to make the site publicly accessible, to be a place for all Singaporeans, to allow our future generations to visit and to foster their own connection to the site.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: There is nothing quite like being in the same place as our forefathers had been, those who had played a key role in our struggle for self-determination.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And in doing so, the NHB will engage potential users of the site, as I have mentioned to other Members before, such as educators and heritage groups, on the different ways in which we can help shape the most appropriate future use of the site for public education purposes.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And if the site is preserved as a National Monument, the site and its historic significance could also be profiled and featured, as part of NHB's efforts to celebrate our National Monuments.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: In terms of different ways and different programs to remind Singaporeans of the significance of the site, I think that these are things that either NHB or the Ministry of Education can subsequently think about and look at.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: But it is our intention to fully allow Singaporeans to really come and appreciate those pivotal events that took place at the site, so that we can enhance our understanding of what it means to be Singaporean and build on our collective and shared identity, so that we can become stronger as a nation.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Will an independent valuation of the site of 38 Oxley Road be done before acquisition?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And will the Government commit to releasing the full evaluation report and provide transparency on the acquisition cost to the public purse?

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: If any owner or person is not satisfied with the compensation awarded, a Notice of Appeal can be filed together with the Land Acquisition Appeals Board, and all these will be taken as part of the due process that is stated under the Land Acquisition Act.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: It is wise to gazette 38 Oxley Road as a National Monument, because if left to free market forces, 38 Oxley Road could be redeveloped into a condominium or a commercial building that will tout it as a prestigious address as the former residence or address of our founding Prime Minister, Mr Lee Kuan Yew, and they can profit from this prestigious address.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I would support the recommendation to remove all traces of Mr Lee and his family's private living space from the building at 38 Oxley Road to respect his wishes.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: While the site has witnessed discussions and meetings that proved to be foundational in the course of Singapore's history, we also recognise that the site was the private residence of Mr Lee and his family.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: And the exact nature of the removal will only be determined subsequently when we are able to access the site and the relevant officers have had a chance to go through, as well as the eventual treatment of the buildings and the structures within the site.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: But I would like to reassure the Member and all Members in this House, that the measures that we are putting in place are not exceptional measures.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: All historic sites, generally, will involve some modifications to some extent, to allow for adaptive reuse, and this also ensures that the site remains something that is beneficial and useful to current and future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: They have all had their interiors somewhat significantly altered, although the exteriors have been preserved.

speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Minister is correct that there will come a day in the future when no living Singaporean remembers the period of independence.

speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Could he share what additional heritage value or visitor experience, beyond the sense of space, would a demolished and subsequently landscaped heritage park at 38 Oxley Road provide, that will not be more effectively delivered through the experience at the $335 million Founders' Memorial, which is purpose-built to honour Singapore's founding values and nation-building journey, including our early nation building years of 1950s to 1970s, and telling the story of how our founding fathers and the founding generation overcame the odds to build an Independent Singapore, establishing it on values and ideals, such as multiculturalism, openness and integrity?

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: I think the answer I had given earlier to another Member, which is that there is something different about being in the same place, where these events took place.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: Like I mentioned in my Ministerial Statement, we have very precious few sites, where there is a confluence of people, events and place.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: It is not the same space where the events took place.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: It is not the same space where the people came together.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: If the preservation were to go through, this site will augment the Founders' Memorial to give Singaporeans a fuller understanding of what it means to be Singaporean, our sense of national identity and how we can forge forward as one people.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: First, I would like to thank the Acting Minister for a heartfelt response to this very difficult topic.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My clarification revolves around how we debated this extensively in 2017, over two days.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Lee had only passed two years prior to that.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Our then-Prime Minister responded and then, then-Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean, at the time, gave what I thought was an excellent conclusion that a future Government, in the fullness of time, on the passage of time, will have to make that decision.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Here we are today and the Minister is now speaking, on behalf of that Government, albeit at an initial stage.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, here I speak and seek clarification that as we move forward, that we realise there are many different interpretations of Mr Lee's wishes and preferences.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And when eventually the Government, the good government of the day, makes this decision, to – I humbly request – be sensitive, be tactful in the explanations, as to why we are doing, or why it is doing what it is doing.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I listened to Ms Chong's question and I also listened to Mr Liang's question, and I think they are both very good questions.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We have a parallel Founders' Memorial, which actually is suppose to give the history, the ethos, the value system of our founding fathers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And I understand that the authenticity of the location of 38 Oxley Road differentiates itself from the Founders' Memorial, but I ask also for a deeper explanation, as the time comes, as to why the Government eventually makes its decision.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And here I say this, with the House's interest at heart, with Singapore's interests at heart and Mr Lee Kuan Yew's interests at heart and overall, the Government's.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I do apologise for going on a little bit more, but for those of us who were not in the House, I can say that it was certainly one of the most difficult speeches I gave.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And we have now come to that situation where we have to make a decision in a future government.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I hope it is done sensitively and tactfully, and with Singaporeans' best interests at heart.

speaker: Mr David Neo
text: So, it is my assurance to the Member that all these things will be taken on board, and the Government will make an informed and responsible decision, for the best of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I understand that due process will be followed for the acquisition.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: I am not sure if that process requires the cost of the land acquisition of 38 Oxley Road to be publicly released.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: But even if not, will the Government commit to still disclose that cost, given the public interest in this matter?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day.
